correctness.rationale: Support elimination is exact: with q fixed, optimize p linearly under mass and two moment constraints, giving an extreme support <=3; then optimize q similarly without lowering global objective. By dihedral action first support reduces to 10 orbits, while the other is any of 92 nonempty supports of size <=3. Each support feasible set is a compact affine-polytope of dimension at most 2. For a quadratic objective, an interior local maximum can be strictly negative-definite stationary or else moved to a smaller-support boundary (if Hessian has nonnegative curvature or a flat stationary direction). The source exact Q(sqrt(2)) verifier was inspected; a separately programmed exact enumerator solved all 920 support pairs, reproduced 126 admissible interior stationary candidates and maximum 13/16-7sqrt(2)/32, independently reconfirming its per-support table. A separate exact enumeration of the 12 extreme individually-zero-mean laws and all 144 pairs gave max 1/2. The explicit 2+3 support witness satisfies mass and collective balance identities exactly.
risk: Exhaustiveness depends on the analytic extreme-support reduction plus compact-face/boundary argument, not simply 920 finite tested distributions.
No classification of all optimal pairs or arbitrary non-affine regular octagons is asserted.
